Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everybody, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — renewals, capacity, eu private pilot, and then technical next steps. how's that sound?
[00:12] Ravi: sounds good. we're, uh, primarily here because traffic spiked Q2 and the DB models are more expensive, so we want a predictable bill and lower tail latency for our inference.
[00:20] Lila: also want to make sure if we commit to a dedicated pool we can get region isolation — EU — we have data residency rules for a subset of customers.
[00:32] Sofia: totally. we've got a couple of patterns — hosted with regional routing, dedicated reserved pools, and private (vpc/on-prem) if you need full control. for the private pilot we recommended a small 3-node cluster in eu-west-1 or on-prem rack depending on network constraints.
[00:47] Owen: just to clarify, when you say on-prem, do you mean a Redwood-managed appliance or an integration we deploy into our row?
[00:55] Ethan: good question — we have both paths. for sensitive workloads the Private model runs a customer-managed control plane; Redwood provides the runtime images and orchestration recipes. for pilots we often do a self-hosted cluster in your cloud account (VPC) — that gives you KMS integration and audit logs without hardware shipping.
[01:10] Owen: okay that matches what we prefer — bring-up in our VPC, KMS keys in our account.
[01:16] Maya: and we'll capture the SSO/SAML integration too so your engs can onboard quickly.
[01:20] Ravi: perfect. quick wrinkle — we evaluated Inferex and Anthropic for a proof of perf; Inferex had aggressive pricing but latency hurt on longer contexts. what's Redwood's position on cost vs latency tradeoffs for reserved capacity?
[01:35] Sofia: right, so with reserved Dedicated capacity you get a predictable hourly commitment and lower p99s because we can tune batching and kernel selection. we also recommend quantized model variants for cheaper token cost; for latency-sensitive routes we can pin a higher-perf model or reserve a lower-batch lane.
[01:49] Lila: can you give a ballpark? last contract we signed with you was 2x nodes, now we anticipate 4–6x during peak. what's the uplift needed to keep p99 under 200ms for our short-chat endpoints?
[02:02] Sofia: initial estimate: if your QPS goes from 50 to 300 with the same request mix, you'll want to go from 2 to around 8 vGPU-equivalent slots for the same p99 profile. but we'll run a benchmark to validate.
[02:15] Ethan: and pricing options — we can do month-to-month with metered overages, or a 12-month reserved commit at a discount (typically 18–25% depending on size). we also have a 24-month with deeper discounts and priority provisioning windows.
[02:30] Ravi: i like the 12-month idea but we need flexibility to scale. can we have burst capacity beyond the commit?
[02:35] Ethan: yes — Reserved plus burst pool: committed baseline for predictable cost plus an on-demand burst that uses hosted capacity at higher unit price. failover routing is automatic.
[02:45] Lila: security/regulatory Q — SOC 2 is fine but can you confirm audit logs are retained for 1 year and that we can export them to our SIEM?
[02:54] Maya: yes, audit logging and long-term retention is part of Private; we can push logs to your logging endpoint, S3, or BigQuery. policy retention and export is configurable.
[03:05] Owen: and KMS — we need keys in our account, HSM-backed if possible.
[03:09] Sofia: supported. we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping; HSM-backed keys depend on provider but we support the common flows.
[03:15] Speaker 1: (inaudible) — sorry, quick aside, are we including embeddings in the commit or only generation tokens?
[03:23] Ethan: good point — we usually separate embedding units since they have different unit economics. we can include a block of embeddings in the committed seats or leave them metered. for Catalyst i propose a hybrid: commit for generation and a small embedding block.
[03:35] Ravi: that's acceptable. next — pilot timeline. can we get an EU pilot live in 2 weeks? our compliance review expects an engineering demo by mid-September.
[03:44] Sofia: 2 weeks is tight but possible; i'll need access to your VPC and network details today or tomorrow to schedule. otherwise we can run a cloud-hosted EU trial in 3–4 days for functional validation while private onboarding completes.
[03:58] Owen: i can share peering configs and egress constraints by Thursday.
[04:02] Lila: on contract length, if we go 12 months with a 20% discount, can we get an SLA credit for p99 > 500ms?
[04:10] Ethan: SLA credits are available on Dedicated and Private tiers; the specifics depend on the commitment and the deployment mode. i'll include an SLA draft in the worksheet.
[04:17] Ravi: benchmark specifics — we want p50 and p99 at 768-token contexts and 4k token contexts; also throughput (tokens/sec) so we can estimate cost per inference.
[04:28] Sofia: noted. for the benchmark we'll include both 768 and 4k runs, pinned and quantized variants, and cold vs warm KV-cache runs. we'll capture latency distrib and token costs.
[04:40] Ethan: quick commercial question: do you need an NDA or PO to start the pilot?
[04:44] Lila: NDA is already in place. PO only for if we commit financially; for the pilot we can run under existing MSA.
[04:50] Maya: i'll attach the MSA link and the pilot SOW template after the call.
[04:55] Ravi: perfect. can we talk about rollback/fallback plans if the private pilot underperforms?
[05:01] Sofia: yes we usually set a canary routing policy: a % of traffic goes to private pilot and the rest hits hosted or dedicated. if latency or errors spike above thresholds we do automated fallback. we can tune thresholds per-route.
[05:13] Owen: how intrusive is the instrumentation? will your agents require kernel modules or special eBPF?
[05:19] Sofia: no kernel modules. we use lightweight agents, standard metrics exporters and optional tracing hooks. nothing that requires deep kernel changes.
[05:27] Ethan: i also want to call out model variants — we can offer a slightly lower-precision quantized variant that reduces cost ~30% but can add 5–7% quality delta; we'll run evals on your prompt set.
[05:38] Ravi: okay we'll provide a 50 prompt eval set and a target metric sheet.
[05:42] Lila: any partner discounts? we occasionally run bench projects with cloud credits.
[05:47] Ethan: we have marketplace and partner credits in some regions; i'll check EU availability and include notes in the worksheet.
[05:55] Speaker 2: (background) — sorry, did you mention support SLAs for weekend on-call?
[05:59] Maya: yes we offer 24/7 support on enterprise tiers and a named CSM. response times vary by tier.
[06:06] Ravi: good. i want to cement costs quickly — can you show incremental pricing: baseline 8 vGPU slots reserved vs 12 vs 16 and projected monthly burn?
[06:16] Ethan: yes that will be in the pricing worksheet. i'll include a model with committed discount tiers and an example month showing burst utilization.
[06:24] Lila: on governance, can we restrict model rollout so only certain teams can push model versions? we need RBAC.
[06:31] Sofia: built-in RBAC and audit trails; you can lock model rollouts to a deployment group and require approval.
[06:37] Owen: network question — we saw token-e2e latency spikes when egress peaked. do you recommend colocated routing or multi-region replication?
[06:45] Sofia: for low latency, multi-region replication with Smart Routing is best. Smart Routing will route to the closest healthy edge; for strict data residency we keep a regional private pool and route EU traffic there.
[06:56] Ravi: what's the break-even on multi-region vs single region?
[06:59] Ethan: depends on traffic shape, but if >30% of traffic originates in EU you often benefit from a dedicated EU pool to avoid cross-region penalties. we'll show a cost model.
[07:08] Lila: can we do a short demo of the console and rollout controls?
[07:11] Sofia: sure — i can share my screen in a follow up. for now quick highlights: per-route latency/cost, token-level breakdown, and rollout gating.
[07:20] Speaker 1: there's some audio glitch — couple seconds delayed.
[07:24] Ethan: apologies. ok, commercial decision — can we tentatively plan for a 12-month renewal with an initial 6-slot uplift (from 2 to 8) and optional mid-year top-up based on benchmarks?
[07:37] Ravi: yes that sounds reasonable provided benchmarks validate p99 under 250ms and cost is within our envelope.
[07:44] Lila: also we need legal to review the SOW for pilot and the MSA addendum for the private deployment.
[07:49] Maya: i'll send the SOW template and an example SOW; legal can redline.
[07:54] Owen: i'll also loop in our networking and security folks once you share the peering checklist.
[07:59] Sofia: great — i'll start the private cluster provisioning once we have network creds; provisioning time is usually 48–72 hours after creds.
[08:07] Ethan: let's pick dates: Ethan will send the pricing worksheet and draft SOW by 2026-09-10; Sofia to provide pilot access by 2026-09-13; benchmark run scheduled week of 2026-09-20. any objections?
[08:19] Ravi: no objections.
[08:21] Lila: none.
[08:23] Ethan: cool. a couple small clarifications — how much traffic will you route to the pilot during the benchmark?
[08:30] Ravi: initially 10% of non-critical traffic, ramp to 30% if stable.
[08:36] Sofia: perfect — that gives good signal without impacting customers.
[08:39] Ethan: okay final items: i'll include competitor notes and why dev experience matters (observability, rollback) in the packet. i'll also include options for embedding block.
[08:48] Ravi: do you have any case studies for EU private pilots?
[08:52] Ethan: yes — i'll share a short one-pager from a EU fintech pilot (redacted).
[08:57] Maya: i'll attach SOC2 and the security questionnaire we've completed.
[09:01] Lila: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:04] Ethan: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the docs and calendar for the benchmark.
[09:09] (call ends)
